cards.front: Worked example: RWA = €1.000m, available own funds €150m, Problemfall Risiko (95% unexpected loss) = €17m. A new SREP P2R of 2% raises the required capital incl. buffers (P1 8% + P2R 2% + CBR 3% = 13%) to €130m, so the freies Kapital (yellow denominator) is €150m − €130m = €20m. Compute the Problemfall Auslastung (Risiko ÷ freies Kapital) as a fraction.

Worked example: available own funds €150m. After the 2% SREP P2R the required capital including buffers (P1+P2R+CBR = 13% of €1.000m RWA) is €130m. Compute the freies Kapital (free capital = own funds − requirement incl. buffers, the Problemfall yellow denominator) in € m.
On RWA = €1.000m with Pillar 1 = 8%, a SREP P2R = 2%, and a combined buffer requirement (CCB+CCyB+SyRB) = 3%, compute the total required capital 'incl. buffers' (P1+P2R+Puffer) in € m.
Within the combined buffer requirement (CBR), the capital conservation buffer (Kapitalerhaltungspuffer) component is fixed at what CET1 rate? Answer as a fraction.

Capital stack, bottom-to-top: Pillar 1 → {{c1}} → combined buffer requirement (CBR) → {{c2}}. The first add-on is binding and sits BELOW the buffers; the second is non-binding and sits ON TOP of the buffers.
Pillar 1 minimum (CRR Art. 92): 8% total own funds, of which {{c1}}% must be CET1 and {{c2}}% Tier 1.

Problemfall traffic light: yellow fires above {{c1}}% utilisation, read against cover INCL. buffers (CRR+P2R+Puffer) — i.e. crossing the MDA line; red fires above {{c2}}%, read against cover EXCL. buffers (CRR+P2R only) — the hard-minimum breach.
Show how a new 2% SREP P2R moves the Problemfall light without touching risk. RWA = €1.000m, own funds €150m, Risiko = €17m.

steps.prompt: After the 2% P2R, what is the required capital incl. buffers (P1 8% + P2R 2% + CBR 3%) on €1.000m RWA?
steps.explain: The P2R raises the requirement from 11% (€110m) to 13% (€130m); the buffers stack on top of P1+P2R.

steps.prompt: What is the freies Kapital (yellow denominator) = own funds − requirement incl. buffers?
steps.explain: Free capital shrinks from €40m (before) to €20m purely through the supervisor's add-on.

steps.prompt: With Risiko = €17m unchanged, what is the Auslastung (Risiko ÷ freies Kapital)?
steps.explain: Up from 42,5%. The P2R moved the DENOMINATOR, not the €17m risk — the normative lens worsens while the Extremfall is untouched.

cards.front: P2R and P2G both come out of the SREP. Someone treats them as interchangeable (both hard, or both soft). Is the distinction regulatory or an ÖRS choice — and what is the actual tradeoff that matters for the Problemfall?
rubric: Both are regulatory in origin (SREP-set under CRD) — this is a reg distinction, not an ÖRS modelling choice
P2R is BINDING and sits BELOW the buffers → a breach is treated like an own-funds shortfall and is MDA-relevant once the combined buffer is eaten
P2G is NON-BINDING and sits ON TOP of the buffers → a breach triggers only a supervisory dialogue, no automatic MDA distribution restriction
Consequence/tradeoff: only P2R (never P2G) enters the Problemfall denominator — the 'inklusive Säule 2 Anforderung, falls von der Aufsicht vorgegeben' clause

cards.front: The Extremfall aggregates material single risks with correlation = +1 (simple addition across risk types). Regulatory requirement or ÖRS choice — and what does it trade off?
rubric: An ÖRS modelling/proportionality choice, NOT a CRR requirement
It is the MOST conservative aggregation — gives away all cross-type diversification benefit (the opposite of a real internal model with corr<1 that REDUCES capital)
Tradeoff: simplicity and defensibility across ~400 banks (and no data to estimate cross-type correlations) vs theoretical fidelity / lower diversified capital
Correlation <1 enters only WITHIN a risk type (e.g. between currencies, between rating classes, Zins↔Credit-Spread inside market risk)

cards.front: CRD Art. 73 / §39a BWG require EVERY institution to run an ICAAP, yet ~400 Primärbanken run one standardised simplified ICAAP rather than bespoke internal economic-capital models. Is the simplified version a breach of the rule or a sanctioned choice — and on what basis?
rubric: Sanctioned, not a breach: the Proportionalitätsgedanke (CRD/EBA proportionality) lets ICAAP DEPTH scale with the institution's size and complexity
The simplification is the ÖRS choice — fixed parameters (M = 2,5; 5% op-risk factor; 5% sonstige-Risiken buffer), pooled data (LGD pool), and corr +1 stand in for bank-specific models
Tradeoff: operational feasibility + statistical robustness (a single small bank has too little data to estimate its own tail/correlations) vs bank-specific precision
It is the licence for every later simplification; the built-in conservatism (e.g. corr +1) buys back the modelling error the simplification introduces

cards.front: An examiner says 'we completed our SREP this quarter.' Correct them: define ICAAP vs SREP, name each legal anchor, and state how the two feed each other.

rubric.text: ICAAP is the BANK's own internal process (CRD Art. 73 → §39a BWG); the bank performs its ICAAP
SREP is the SUPERVISOR's review/scoring (CRD Art. 97, ECB/SSM or FMA/OeNB); the supervisor does the SREP TO the bank, so 'we did our SREP' is wrong
The SREP scores four blocks (business model, governance, capital risk, liquidity & funding risk) and outputs the Pillar-2 add-ons P2R and P2G
The ÖRS Leitfaden/RTFA IS the sector's standardised ICAAP; the ICAAP feeds the SREP, the SREP feeds back the add-on the ICAAP must respect

antiPoints: Says the bank performs the SREP on itself
Swaps the legal anchors (Art. 97 for ICAAP / Art. 73 for SREP)
Claims ICAAP and SREP are two names for the same exercise
cards.modelAnswer: You run the ICAAP — the bank's own Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (CRD Art. 73, transposed in §39a BWG) — self-assessing that capital covers all material risks under both perspectives. The supervisor (ECB/SSM for a significant institution like RBI, otherwise FMA/OeNB) runs the SREP — the Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process (CRD Art. 97) — scoring business model, governance, capital risk and liquidity & funding risk, and from that sets the Pillar-2 add-ons P2R (binding) and P2G (guidance). So 'we did our SREP' is wrong: you do your ICAAP, the supervisor does the SREP to you. The ICAAP feeds the SREP and the SREP feeds back the add-on the ICAAP must then respect; in our sector the standardised Leitfaden is that ICAAP.

cards.front: Defend the mapping 'normative ↔ Problemfall, economic ↔ Extremfall' to the Aufsichtsrat — and say precisely where the analogy breaks.

rubric.text: Normative perspective = can we meet ALL regulatory/supervisory demands (P1+P2R+buffers, P2G soft) continuously, multi-year, baseline + adverse → maps to the Problemfall
Economic perspective = the bank's own internal view of all material risks at its own (higher) confidence, here 99,9% → maps to the Extremfall
It is an ANALOGY, not an identity: the ECB normative view is genuine multi-year capital planning, but the Problemfall compresses it into a one-year, 95% unexpected-loss quantile
Second gap: the Extremfall is at 99,9% but deliberately conservative (corr +1), not the ECB's diversified internal model

antiPoints: States the Problemfall IS the ECB's full normative perspective
Claims the Problemfall is a multi-year planning exercise
Swaps the confidence levels (calls the economic view 95% / the normative view 99,9%)
cards.modelAnswer: The ECB ICAAP requires two perspectives in parallel: a normative view — can we continuously meet all regulatory and supervisory capital demands (Pillar 1 + P2R + buffers, with P2G as a soft target) over a multi-year horizon under baseline and adverse scenarios — and an economic view — is there enough substance against our own, fuller, higher-confidence picture of all material risks. The normative view maps to the Problemfall and the economic view to the Extremfall at 99,9%. But it is an analogy, not an identity: the ECB's normative perspective is a genuine multi-year capital-planning exercise, whereas our Problemfall compresses it into a one-year, 95% unexpected-loss quantile against a one-year Deckungsmasse; and our Extremfall, though at 99,9%, is a deliberately conservative correlation-+1 construction rather than a diversified internal model. I would present both mappings as conceptual bridges and flag those two gaps when challenged.

cards.front: An examiner challenges: 'your Extremfall is an economic-capital model, so it should hand you a diversification benefit.' Respond.

rubric.text: Reject the premise: the Extremfall is economic in SCOPE (all material risks: Beteiligungs-, makroökonomisches, Konzentrations-, Zinsänderungsrisiko) and CONFIDENCE (own 99,9%) and own parameters — not in claiming diversification
It aggregates with correlation = +1 (simple addition), the most conservative possible — the OPPOSITE of a diversified internal model that uses corr<1 to reduce capital
This is a deliberate ÖRS proportionality trade: simplicity/defensibility over theoretical fidelity (it gives away diversification benefit on purpose)
Correlation <1 enters only WITHIN a risk type (currencies, rating classes, Zins↔Credit-Spread)

antiPoints: Accepts that the Extremfall claims cross-type diversification
Describes the Extremfall as a diversified internal model
Treats correlation +1 as a CRR requirement rather than an ÖRS choice
cards.modelAnswer: I'd push back on the premise. Our Extremfall is 'economic' in that it widens the risk scope to all material risks Pillar 1 omits (Beteiligungs-, makroökonomisches, Konzentrations- and Zinsänderungsrisiko), lifts confidence to our own uniform 99,9%, and uses our own parameters — but it deliberately does NOT claim diversification. It aggregates the material single risks with correlation = +1, i.e. simple addition, which is the most conservative possible treatment and the exact opposite of a real internal model that uses correlations below 1 to reduce capital. That is a conscious ÖRS proportionality trade — simplicity and defensibility over theoretical fidelity, giving away diversification benefit on purpose, which also buys back the modelling error the simplification introduces. Correlation below 1 enters only within a single risk type, e.g. between currencies, between rating classes, or between interest-rate and credit-spread risk inside market risk.
